key_insight: Agent-screened pathology images support a generative model whose learned representations transfer to cell segmentation.
clinical_relevance: The framework could support pathology image analysis when pixel-level annotations are scarce, but clinical utility is not established in the abstract.
method: Use a pathology agent system to assess image quality and screen TCGA patches.
Train a generative backbone for image synthesis and structural and semantic representation learning.
Adapt the pretrained backbone to semantic segmentation with a lightweight task-specific head.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 217,030 screened TCGA patches, expert annotations for approximately 380,000 cells across 12 types, and state-of-the-art segmentation results on multiple pathology datasets, without numerical metrics.
watch_item: Generalization across laboratories and staining protocols requires further validation before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Agent-Driven Generative Priors for Pathology Image Synthesis and Segmentation
